mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility improves from -3.9 to -1.1 over four weeks, indicating commuters return to offices; this raises weekday retail footfall and pushes RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES remaining above -2.0 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stays below -12 for three consecutive weeks, showing constrained movement; this limits discretionary trips and keeps RETAIL_REC below its last-28-day mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean remains below -12 for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT remains below -12 for three consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL above 6.0 together with GROCERY_PHARM above -10.0 signals home-centered routines; fewer trips are allocated to discretionary retail, so RETAIL_REC falls below its last-28-day mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean >= 6.0 and GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean >= -10.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean when RESIDENTIAL >= 6.0 and GROCERY_PHARM >= -10.0.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility rebounds by at least 2 points week-on-week, drawing discretionary leisure time outdoors and substituting away from indoor retail; RETAIL_REC declines relative to its last-28-day mean within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises by >= 2.0 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its last-28-day mean when PARKS rises by at least 2.0 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A WORKPLACES crossing above -2.0 for two consecutive weeks marks policy relaxation; office and commute activity return, lifting RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean > -2.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean after WORKPLACES exceeds -2.0 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stabilizing at or above -13.5 and WORKPLACES at or above -2.0 jointly signal broader reopening; combined commuter and transit recovery raises RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean >= -13.5 and WORKPLACES weekly mean >= -2.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last-28-day mean when TRANSIT >= -13.5 and WORKPLACES >= -2.0.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improves from -10.7 to -9.0, indicating stock-up trips normalize; routine shopping resumes and lifts RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains above -10.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a residential-elevated regime where RESIDENTIAL is at least 6.0, high home time suppresses retail even if TRANSIT is stable; RETAIL_REC stays below its last-28-day mean over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL >= 6.0.
